title: The Guest House: Rumi on Welcoming Every Feeling
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi's Guest House | 8 Persian Sufi Poems on Sorrow, Joy and Every Feeling (English Translation)
intro: Rumi once compared the human body to a guest house.
Every morning a new guest arrives: a joy, a sorrow, a sudden worry.
Here are eight passages from his Masnavi about how to receive them.

poems.name: The Guest House

lines.fa: هست مهمان‌خانه این تن ای جوان
lines.en: This body is a guest house, young friend:

lines.fa: هر صباحی ضیف نو آید دوان
lines.en: every morning a new guest comes running.

lines.fa: هین مگو کین ماند اندر گردنم
lines.en: Do not say, "This one will hang on my neck forever,"

lines.fa: که هم اکنون باز پرد در عدم
lines.en: for right now it flies back into nothingness.

tafsir: This is the passage that gave our channel its name.
Rumi is talking about the thoughts and moods that arrive in us each day.
When a hard feeling comes, we often fear it will stay forever.
Rumi says no. It is a guest, and guests leave.
Even the heaviest mood is already on its way out.

poems.name: A Guest from the Unseen

lines.fa: هرچه آید از جهان غیب‌وش
lines.en: Whatever comes from the unseen world

lines.fa: در دلت ضیفست او را دار خوش
lines.en: into your heart is a guest. Treat it kindly.

tafsir: We do not choose what feelings come to us.
They arrive from somewhere we cannot see.
Rumi does not ask us to like every guest.
He asks us to be a good host.
To let the feeling sit down, instead of slamming the door.

poems.name: Sorrow Sweeps the House

lines.fa: فکر غم گر راه شادی می‌زند
lines.en: If the thought of sorrow blocks the road to joy,

lines.fa: کارسازیهای شادی می‌کند
lines.en: it is preparing the way for joy.

lines.fa: خانه می‌روبد به تندی او ز غیر
lines.en: It sweeps the house roughly clean of everything else,

lines.fa: تا در آید شادی نو ز اصل خیر
lines.en: so that a new joy can enter from the source of good.

tafsir: A few lines later Rumi looks more closely at one guest: sorrow.
Sorrow can feel like a thief that takes our happiness.
Rumi sees it as a cleaner.
It empties the rooms, sometimes roughly,
so that there is space for something new to come in.

poems.name: Yellow Leaves

lines.fa: می‌فشاند برگ زرد از شاخ دل
lines.en: It shakes the yellow leaves from the branch of the heart,

lines.fa: تا بروید برگ سبز متصل
lines.en: so that green leaves can grow, one after another.

lines.fa: می‌کند بیخ سرور کهنه را
lines.en: It pulls up the root of an old happiness,

lines.fa: تا خرامد ذوق نو از ما ورا
lines.en: so that a new delight can walk in from beyond.

tafsir: Here the heart is a tree in autumn.
Grief shakes it, and the old leaves fall.
It looks like loss, and it is loss.
But Rumi asks us to notice what the falling makes room for.
Some joys must end before new ones can begin.

poems.name: The Cloud

lines.fa: ابر را گر هست ظاهر رو ترش
lines.en: The cloud may have a frowning face,

lines.fa: گلشن آرنده‌ست ابر و شوره‌کش
lines.en: yet the cloud brings gardens and washes away the salt.

lines.fa: فکر غم را تو مثال ابر دان
lines.en: Think of the thought of sorrow as a cloud,

lines.fa: با ترش تو رو ترش کم کن چنان
lines.en: and do not frown back at the one who frowns.

tafsir: A dark cloud does not look friendly.
But without it, nothing grows.
Rumi gives us a gentle piece of advice here.
When a sad thought arrives with a sour face, do not answer it with anger.
Meet it calmly. It may be bringing rain.

poems.name: Unless the Cloud Weeps

lines.fa: تا نگرید ابر کی خندد چمن
lines.en: Until the cloud weeps, how will the meadow laugh?

lines.fa: تا نگرید طفل کی جوشد لبن
lines.en: Until the baby cries, how will the milk begin to flow?

lines.fa: طفل یک روزه همی‌داند طریق
lines.en: Even a one-day-old child knows the way:

lines.fa: که بگریم تا رسد دایهٔ شفیق
lines.en: "I will cry, so that the kind nurse comes."

tafsir: These lines come from the very beginning of Book Five.
Rumi is speaking about tears.
We often treat crying as weakness, something to hide.
For Rumi, tears are a call, like a baby calling for its mother.
Weeping is how help, and mercy, find their way to us.

poems.name: Contraction and Expansion

lines.fa: چونک قبض آید تو در وی بسط بین
lines.en: When the heart contracts, see the opening within it.

lines.fa: تازه باش و چین میفکن در جبین
lines.en: Stay fresh, and do not let your brow fall into a frown.

tafsir: Sufis speak of two states of the heart: qabz and bast.
Qabz is contraction, the heart closing like a fist.
Bast is expansion, the heart opening wide.
Rumi says that even inside the closing, the opening is already waiting.
Like breathing in, before breathing out.

poems.name: When You See Sorrow

lines.fa: چونک غم بینی تو استغفار کن
lines.en: When you see sorrow, ask for forgiveness;

lines.fa: غم بامر خالق آمد کارکن
lines.en: sorrow came at the Creator's command, and it is at work.

lines.fa: چون بخواهد عین غم شادی شود
lines.en: When He wills, sorrow itself becomes joy,

lines.fa: عین بند پای آزادی شود
lines.en: the very chain on the foot becomes freedom.

tafsir: Our last passage comes from the first book of the Masnavi.
Rumi says that sorrow does not come by accident. It has work to do.
And the same thing that binds us can become the thing that frees us.
So the guest we feared most may be the one who sets us free.
Open the door. Every guest has been sent from beyond.

outro: Thank you for staying with these verses.
